svg.text: The story model at a glance
Using Chapters 1–2 of 86—EIGHTY-SIX as the example. A story model is everything a reader knows after a given section, and every
piece of it leads back to the text.
What is inside: entities, claims about them, and evidence
Entities: the “who / where / which group” of the story
An entity is only an ID and a kind (Shin is c006). Its names and everything else about it are the claims below.
Claims: seven kinds, each shown here with Shin
how A relates to B; it has a
the order the book tells it
two entities may be the same
Claims point to entities by ID:
Every claim carries evidence: which section + which paragraph + an exact quote
Example: the name “Shinei Nouzen” ← Chapter 2 (section-005) · paragraph p0012 · “Shin! Shinei Nouzen! Ya fucked it all up again…”
Two labels: how do we know, and when does it hold?
Relationships and events carry both; attributes and identity links only “how do we know”; names, aliases, and questions carry neither.
Shin is the Spearhead squadron’s captain
a character or in-world source says it; it may
be false, and the speaker is recorded
Karlstahl: Handlers call him the Reaper; he
not said outright, but it follows from the text
Annette is an Alba, from “her short hair was
Lena is appointed Handler of the Spearhead
Nine years earlier, the Empire of Giad started
The Republic expects every Legion unit to
Raiden thinks: born in the age of knights, Shin
would be the hero of a myth *
the text does not say when
The two labels are independent and combine freely: a story told by a character about the old days is reported + past. Examples marked * are illustrations:
the sentence is from these chapters, but the current model has no such record.
Reading on, section by section: claims are added, never deleted
Gray: the old claim stays in the file, inactive
Green: the claim that is active now
a new claim replaces an older one about the same thing, like the name and age above
a later section shows an old claim was wrong; it is withdrawn with no replacement
an open question gets its answer (not yet in these chapters)
Old claims are never deleted, only no longer active. So in the app, Shin shows as Undertaker at Chapter 1 and as Shinei Nouzen at
Chapter 2, and Raiden, who first appears in Chapter 2, stays hidden at Chapter 1.
